title: Tenant Routing Admin API — proto & notes
content:
Quick brain-dump / working draft of a lightweight admin API for per-tenant routing policies. Goal: provide a single, auditable surface for product/platform to bind routing rules (region, tier, fallback, cost-priority) to tenant IDs; make runtime decision deterministic and debuggable.

Context / why:
- We currently have routing rules split across: per-team YAML committed to infra repo, runtime heuristics, and some hard-coded fallbacks in serving. Hard to reason about tenant-level overrides (especially dedicated vs hosted).
- Operational ask: allow SRE/customer-success to set tenant-specific overrides (e.g., force tenant to use dedicated, or pin to a model family), and have those changes take effect within minutes without service restarts.

Requirements (high-level):
- CRUD for tenant routing policy (per-tenant object).
- Policy resolution order: explicit tenant policy -> team policy -> global default.
- Strong auditing, who/when changed what (immutable revisions).
- Soft rollout: support canary percentage on a policy (apply to a X% of requests for the tenant).
- Validation: ensure policy is compatible with tenant product tier (e.g., cannot pin to private model if tenant not on Private plan).
- Fast propagation: control plane to runtime delta push; optional TTL-based polling fallback.
- Backwards compatible with current heuristics; if no policy exists, runtime must continue current behavior.

API surface (REST / HTTP admin):
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing-policies  -> create new policy (returns policy id, revision)
- GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing-policies[?rev] -> retrieve active or specific revision
- PUT /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing-policies/{policy_id} -> update (creates new revision)
- DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing-policies/{policy_id} -> soft-delete (marks as revoked)
- GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing-policies/revisions -> list revisions (paginated)
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing-policies/{policy_id}/apply-preview -> dry-run returning matching decisions for a sample of recent request traces
- GET /v1/routing/resolve?tenant_id=...&request_meta=... -> debug-only endpoint to run the resolution algorithm and return the decision tree (for UI / SRE)

Policy schema (informal):
- id: string (uuid)
- tenant_id: string
- created_by: string (email)
- created_at: timestamp (iso)
- status: active | revoked | pending
- matchers: list of matchers (optional). If empty -> apply to all requests for tenant. Matchers can restrict to route by product, environment, region, model call-type (chat/generation/embeddings), sequence_len_bucket.
- route: object (one-of):
    - force_model: { model_family: string, model_version: string (optional), quantization_profile: string (optional)}
    - prefer_capacity_tier: { tier: hosted | dedicated | private, fallback_to: list }
    - weighted_pool_routing: [ {pool_id: string, weight: int} ]
- canary: { enabled: bool, percent: int }
- expires_at: timestamp (optional)
- metadata: freeform map (owner reference, jira, notes)

Notes on schema decisions:
- Putting matchers on the policy allows attaching a small set of conditional overrides (e.g., small embeddings jobs go to hosted, large chat to dedicated).
- route is intentionally flexible; runtime will validate supported route shapes.
- metadata should be freeform but surfaced in UI and audit logs.

Examples (pseudo-JSON request bodies):
1) Pin tenant to dedicated pool with canary:
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-inc",
  "route": { "prefer_capacity_tier": { "tier": "dedicated", "fallback_to": ["hosted"] } },
  "canary": { "enabled": true, "percent": 10 },
  "metadata": { "jira": "ENG-3312", "requested_by": "support@acme.com" }
}

2) Weighted routing between two pools for embedding calls:
{
  "tenant_id": "pm-team",
  "matchers": [ { "call_type": "embeddings" } ],
  "route": { "weighted_pool_routing": [ {"pool_id": "pool-a", "weight": 70}, {"pool_id": "pool-b", "weight": 30} ] }
}

Runtime semantics (sketch):
- Control plane stores policies in authoritative DB (append-only revisions).
- Control plane pushes deltas over pub/sub (Kafka-ish) to regional runtime control caches. Fallback: runtime polls an /sync endpoint with last-known-rev.
- Runtime on decision: take request, extract tenant_id -> fetch tenant-policy from local cache (if any) -> run matcher list in order -> if matched, apply route shape to produce target (model id/pool) -> else apply team/global heuristics.
- If route specifies prefer_capacity_tier: runtime will attempt to allocate from indicated pool(s) using existing capacity allocator. If not allocable, honor fallback list. If none, fall back to existing default.

Propagation and rollout:
- New policy revisions enter state pending. When set to active (either by API or via automated approval), control plane pushes to region(s). Propagation target: 95th percentile < 2m; eventual consistency ok for 5m window.
- Canary semantics: policy engine should attach randomness seeded by request-id so a tenant wide 10% applies consistently for same request pattern during the canary window.

Access control / audit:
- Only RBAC roles with routing:update can create/update. UI shows diffs between revisions.
- Each revision must store who initiated and an optional review ticket id.
- Audit log export endpoint for compliance (CSV/JSON) filtered by tenant/team/date range.

Testing and observability:
- Expose metrics: routing.policy.evaluations{outcome=(applied|skipped|failed)}, routing.policy.latency, routing.policy.canary_assigned_count, routing.resolve.debug_count.
- Add a sampling profiler for resolve endpoint to capture the matched branch and policy_id. Emit structured event to tracing span.
- Provide a debug log option for single tenant to emit policy evaluation logs for N requests.

Operational playbooks (rough):
- Roll forward: apply policy in pending -> enable canary 5% -> monitor errors/latency for 24 hours -> increase to 50% -> full.
- Rollback: revoke policy (soft-delete) -> control plane marks revision revoked and pushes tombstone -> runtime should stop applying; previous revision becomes active.

Edge cases & open questions (TODOs):
- How do we represent time-windowed policies? Need expires_at + activation window. Do we support cron-like schedules? (TODO: capture SRE ask).
- How to avoid conflict between inline matchers and global model-compatibility constraints (e.g., customer using a model that's private). We need validator hooks tied to billing/tenant_entitlements.
- Should UI allow editing raw policy JSON or provide a guided form only? Probably both, with validation.
- Multi-tenant or team-level bulk edits: provide bulk import API and dry-run preview.
- Policy size limits: we should limit total matchers & rules to keep evaluation cheap. Suggest 20 matchers max.
- Canary determinism: need to define seed (request_id, tenant_id, timestamp bucket?).

Migration plan (from current heuristics):
1) Create a read-only export that converts current heuristics into initial tenant-level policies (for a subset of tenants).
2) Run in dry-run preview mode for 48 hours and compare divergence metrics.
3) If divergence tolerated, enable policy in canary for small percentage and monitor.
4) Gradually roll out and then retire old code paths when coverage > 95% and no regressions.

UX wireframe (ascii):
[Admin UI] --(PUT policy)--> [Control plane DB (revisions)] --(pubsub delta)--> [Regional policy caches] --> [Serving runtime routers]
                                    ^
                                    |\\
                                (audit stream)

Small decision trace example (debug/resolve endpoint):
resolve(tenant=acme, call_type=chat, region=us-east) =>
  found policy revision f3a9
  matcher #0 matched (call_type=chat)
  route -> prefer_capacity_tier(dedicated)
  allocation attempted on pool-dedicated-42 -> success
  decision: target=pool-dedicated-42, model=latest-redwood-chat-v2

Implementation notes (practical):
- Start with REST admin API + Postgres revisions table + Redis regional cache + Kafka delta stream (we have these infra pieces).
- Validation service should be a lightweight lambda that can call billing/tenant-entitlement. Could be synchronous at write-time.
- For canary assignment: implement via consistent hashing modulo 100 using HMAC(request_id, policy_revision) to get deterministic bucket.

Docs & follow-ups (action items):
- Draft OpenAPI spec for the endpoints above (blocked: need decision on matchers DSL). @Maya to spin up initial OpenAPI stub.
- Add schema contract for route object and validation hooks.
- Create a small prototype that pushes policy -> cache -> runtime with a simple resolve debug endpoint. Aim: POC in 2 weeks.
- Create a confluence page for playbooks and revive related Jira ENG-1283.

Notes-to-self: keep policy shapes conservative to avoid overloading the runtime with complex rules. Avoid embedding heavy expressions. Prefer declarative matchers (equals/in/list/range).

Unresolved UX bits: whether to expose 'preview' dry-run by default in the UI and how to sample traces without leaking PII. Need privacy review.

Slack threads and refs: #platform-routing, #sre-oncall.

-- end of scratchpad --

(If this doc looks worth keeping, will move to shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering and create a proper OpenAPI/PR.)
